Alternative 5: Rather than propose this legislation, the Secretary might continue administration of the program under the present authority. This would constitute the "no action" alternative. Among the measures that would be foregone if the proposed legislation was not enacted would be the following:
(1) There would be no provision for protection and management of species before they become threatened with extinction.
(2) There would be no responsibility placed on Federal Agencies besides the Departments of Interior, Agriculture, and Defense.
(3) There would be no authority for import agents to inspect wildlife shipment in the "no trade zone" in the course of transshipment.
(4) There would be no authority to acquire lands with Land and Water Conservation Funds.
(5) There would be no authority to prevent U.S. projects in foreign countries from threatening endangered species.
(6) There would be no Federal protection of non-migratory endangered species.
(7) There would be no authority to control exports of endangered species.
Enactment of the above provisions would considerably strengthen the capability of the Secretary to maintain an effective program of endangered species management, both foreign and native. Species could be added to the present endangered list more readily as needed. Programs could then be enacted to prevent such species from reaching Group 1 status.
